answer: A sybil swarm fails when each identity must run a registered jade assay laboratory: a lantern-lit bench where a certified assayer tests a physical jade sample, with signed X-ray fluorescence spectra streamed to the network and cross-checked against the lab's horizon-line geolocation and neighbouring labs. Faking one identity costs a separate lab, certified assayer, spectrometer and lease — a real-world price per fake that no script can clone.
